intro: Tsagarada is a cluster of stone hamlets on the wooded eastern slope of Mount Pelion, in Greece, above the Aegean. In the square of Agia Paraskevi a huge plane tree shades the cafe tables, one of its great limbs carried on a stone pillar. A reader sent us three photographs of it, taken after dark with its branches lit from below, and puts its age at about a thousand years.

trees.name: The Plane of Agia Paraskevi
trees.age_estimate: about 1,000 years, by a reader's estimate
trees.story:
In the square of Agia Paraskevi, in the Pelion mountain village of Tsagarada, the cafe tables stand under a plane tree of enormous girth. A reader sent us three photographs of it, taken after dark with the branches lit from below.

The photographs show why people stop. The trunk comes up out of a stone-edged bed set into the paving, and from it the limbs leave almost sideways, thick as trunks themselves, and run out over the chairs. One of them rests on a square pillar of stacked stone, and another ends in a wide, rounded wound where an old branch was taken off. Where the light catches it, the bark shows in grey and cream patches, and the last autumn leaves hang gold in the crown.

The reader gives it as about a thousand years old, with a girth of 14 to 15 metres, and says the trunk starts four metres below the square's paving. Those are their figures, not a measurement we have seen. A tree of this kind is hard to date, and we would like to hear from anyone who has counted or measured it.

Go in the evening, when the square's lamps come on, and walk all the way round the pillar to see how the great limb is held.
trees.how_to_recognise: A vast plane in the middle of the village square, rising from a stone-edged bed in the paving, with one great limb resting on a square pillar of stacked stone and cafe tables beneath.

question_meta: The giant plane in the square of Agia Paraskevi, Tsagarada, on Mount Pelion: what it looks like, where it stands and what readers say of its age.
question_answer: The Plane of Agia Paraskevi stands in the village square of Agia Paraskevi in Tsagarada, on Mount Pelion. It is in the open square among the cafe tables, free to see at any hour.
question_context: A reader sent us three photographs of this plane tree in the square of Agia Paraskevi, in Tsagarada on Mount Pelion. The tree is an oriental plane, Platanus orientalis. In the photographs, taken after dark, the trunk rises from a stone-edged bed set into the paving and gives way almost at once to limbs as thick as trunks, which run out sideways over the cafe chairs. One rests on a square pillar of stacked stone, and another ends in a wide, rounded wound where an old branch was cut away. Lamps and floodlights pick out the grey and cream patches of the bark and the last gold leaves of the crown. The reader puts the tree at about a thousand years old, with a girth of 14 to 15 metres, and says the trunk starts four metres below the paving of the square. Those figures are theirs; we have not seen a measurement or a register entry for the tree. It stands in the middle of the square, so the way to see it is to sit down at one of the tables beneath it, or walk round the pillar and the bed at its foot.

faq.q: Can I visit The Plane of Agia Paraskevi?
faq.a: Yes. It stands in the village square of Agia Paraskevi in Tsagarada, among the cafe tables, and the square is open at any hour.
